'''Open Web Analytics (OWA)''' is  [[open-source software|open-source]] web analytics software created by Peter Adams. 

OWA is written in [[PHP]] and uses a [[MySQL]] database, which makes it compatible for running with an [[List of AMP packages|AMP]] [[solution stack]] on various [[web server]]s.<ref>{{cite web |title=Open Web Analytics |url=http://www.openwebanalytics.com/ |accessdate=16 February 2012}}</ref> 

==Overview==
OWA is comparable to [[Google Analytics]], though OWA is server software anyone can install and run on their own host, while Google Analytics is a [[Software as a service|software service]] offered by Google.<ref name="comp">{{cite web|title=Comparison|url=http://www.openwebanalytics.com/?page_id=158|work=Open Web Analytics|accessdate=16 February 2012}}</ref> 

OWA supports tracking with [[WordPress]] and [[MediaWiki]], two popular website frameworks.<ref>{{cite web|title=About|url=http://www.openwebanalytics.com/?page_id=2|work=Open Web Analytics|accessdate=16 February 2012}}</ref> This application helps [[webmaster]]s keep track of and observe the influx of views on their websites.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-01-01 |title=Web Content Accessibility Guidelines WCAG 2.2 |url=https://contentplanning.ai/wcag-2-2/ |access-date=2026-05-29}}</ref>

The program also tracks the websites of competitors and their company's growth compared to the site in question.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.ardormediafactory.com/do-i-need-open-web-analytics|title=What is Open Analytics and Do I Need it?|date=5 August 2015|accessdate=5 August 2015}}</ref>
